subject: mathematics

applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public PYP page describes the programme as education for children aged 3-12. Mapping that span to Grade 2 (often about ages 7-8) is our convention, not an IB grade boundary.

grade_specific_note.label: C
grade_specific_note.text: Grade 2 Florida work is still mostly addition and subtraction, with even and odd numbers and repeated addition as an early look at multiplication. That is narrower than the grade 3 library's multiplication-and-division note.

subject_group_or_structure.mapping_to_primer_subject: The grade 3 library treats PYP Mathematics as number, pattern and function, data handling, measurement, and shape and space, taught through inquiry. That strand list is reused. Public pages retrieved today confirm subject-specific learning inside units of inquiry, not these five strand names.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: PYP Mathematics scope and sequence, as recorded in the grade 3 library, covers five strands: Number, Pattern and function, Data handling, Measurement, and Shape and space.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Mathematical learning, as recorded in the grade 3 library, is described through constructing meaning, transferring meaning, and applying with understanding. No grade-2 phase was verified.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 2 Florida mathematics in this draft emphasizes three-digit place value, addition and subtraction within 100 with exploration to 1,000, equal parts of shapes, length, time, money, two-dimensional figures, perimeter, and data displays. Those are Florida benchmarks. A PYP fit is using number, measurement, shape, and data inside a unit of inquiry, without claiming IB sets the same limits (for example, rounding only from 0 to 100).

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Reading and writing numbers to 1,000 fits the reused Number strand. The 1,000 ceiling is Florida's, not an IB grade rule.
Addition and subtraction within 100 can be applying understanding. Procedural reliability is Florida language.

Naming halves, thirds, and fourths of circles and rectangles is an early fraction idea under Number. Florida says not to require numerator and denominator in the clarification, which is not copied here as an IB rule.
Measuring length with inch, foot, yard, centimeter, or meter fits the reused Measurement strand.
Identifying and drawing named polygons fits Shape and space and the concept of form.
Tally marks, tables, pictographs, and bar graphs fit the reused Data handling strand.
One- and two-step real-world problems fit the public emphasis on learning in context.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
